key_insight: Adding clouds and phase transitions changes inverse energy transfer in rotating-stratified turbulence, weakening the upscale cascade and organizing coherent moist PV structures along fuzzy phase boundaries.
engineering_relevance: This matters for atmospheric flow modeling because moist processes can alter large-scale circulation, energy pathways, and the formation of coherent updrafts and downdrafts in geophysical simulations.
method: Numerical simulations of an idealized Boussinesq rotating-stratified flow with random forcing
Moist extension includes water vapor, liquid water, and fast cloud microphysics with separate unsaturated and saturated Froude numbers
Energy transfer and coherence are analyzed through pseudo potential vorticity, buoyancy energies, and cloud-indicator phase boundaries
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that, for fixed Rossby and dry Froude numbers, the moist case shows reduced inverse energy transfer compared with dry dynamics, with coherent structures aligned to time-averaged cloud boundaries.
watch_item: The conclusions are drawn from an idealized model with asymptotically fast microphysics, so real-cloud parameterizations and slower phase-change dynamics may shift the transfer behavior.
paper_title: Inverse Transfer and Coherence in Rotating Stratified Flow with Clouds and Phase Transitions
